why: An order of two values whose shape is the primitive string reads StrLt in the heap core, whatever type spells the string (design/heap-stage5.md 8b, the union-order case read 2026-10-31): a union of string literals and a branded string are their string at run time, as a string enum's member is. Before, the heap checker tested the operands' StringLike flag alone, which a union and an intersection do not carry, and the units stayed out of the core. levelOrder: b > a for a < b over a literal union (proved). dropped: the candidate allocates a record it drops, then orders the copied field (proved up to the dropped allocation, the canonical heap reading, which only a unit in the heap core has; the whole heap differs by the cell). strict: <= for < (unproved, WITNESS at a == b). idOrder: b > a for a < b over a branded string (proved).
